weaknesses: The central claim of geometrically consistent 3D generation is insufficiently evaluated. FID, KID, and LPIPS on projected images measure appearance, not geometric accuracy or consistency across generated viewpoints. There are no quantitative tests of point-cloud quality, camera adherence, preservation of observed geometry, or consistency across multiple target views. Encoder depth results do not validate generated geometry.

The generation baselines are inadequate for establishing superiority. CUT3R and LVSM do not provide a strong comparison against generative single-image scene completion, and their adaptation, training data, and input settings are insufficiently documented. A competitive pose-conditioned generative baseline, including novel-view image generation followed by MASt3R reconstruction, would help establish the value of generating geometric-semantic features.

The benefit of unification is not isolated. The understanding-only encoder evaluation actually achieves higher VSI/BLINK scores than the full model: 42.18/44.40 versus 40.1/43.6. Encoder freezing differs between these configurations, so this does not establish negative transfer, but it leaves the tradeoff unresolved. Understanding generated content is assessed only through qualitative captions.

The main VQA comparisons confound architecture with spatial instruction tuning: UniUGG receives SPAR and other task-specific training, without corresponding matched training for the comparison models. Technical inconsistencies impede reproducibility. Table 4 describes KL divergence as the mean log variance, which is not the Gaussian KL objective stated in the text. Appendix A.2 specifies 768 encoder tokens, whereas the VAE architecture assumes 196, without explaining the conversion. These may be documentation errors, but the actual implementation needs clarification.

Evaluation protocols remain underspecified. The 0.25M generation evaluation samples are described as separate from training, but scene-level disjointness is not established; distinct image pairs from the same scan would not demonstrate unseen-scene generalization. Viewpoint sampling, baseline fine-tuning, joint loss weighting, and uncertainty estimates are also missing. Together with the absent geometric validation and stronger generative comparisons, these gaps place the submission below the acceptance threshold.
